Status

FinKore Core 2.0.4 stable.

Purpose

Approval Composition combines Requirements into groups, quorum decisions, and ordered stages, with limited nesting. It extends Approval Chains.

Reading path (Non-Normative)

Start with the group kinds below, then the requirements. For detailed evaluation, follow quorum evidence, thresholds, inapplicable groups, and stages. Complete validation explains why a decisive outcome does not bypass checks on the rest of the definition. Examples illustrate how the parts fit together.

Terminology

An Approval Composition is an evaluation definition made from Approval Requirements, Approval Groups, and optionally ordered Approval Stages.

An Approval Group is a bounded set of members combined by one of these group kinds:

KindMeaning when members apply
ALL_OFEvery applicable member's approval is needed
ANY_OFAt least one applicable member's approval is needed
N_OF_MAt least N distinct declared voters' effective approvals are needed

A group member is either a declared Approval Requirement reference or a declared child Approval Group reference, subject to the quorum-specific restriction below. An N_OF_M member references an Approval Requirement and explicitly names one voter Actor identity. Each declared voter occurs once within that quorum group; its applicable members therefore represent distinct potential voters. A currently effective Decision can contribute only to the member declaring its Actor and referencing its Requirement. Declaring a voter does not establish eligibility.

ALL_OF and ANY_OF may contain child quorum groups. A quorum group cannot itself contain child groups as voting members.

Requirements

Definition and nesting

  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-001 — An Approval Composition MUST declare exactly one root Approval Group or one nonempty ordered list of Approval Stages. Each Stage MUST declare one or more root Approval Group references, and each reference MUST resolve to exactly one declared Approval Group.
  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-002 — Every Approval Group MUST have a stable identifier that is unique within the Approval Composition.
  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-003 — Every Approval Group MUST declare exactly one group kind: ALL_OF, ANY_OF, or N_OF_M.
  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-004 — Every Approval Group MUST contain one or more declared members, and every member reference MUST resolve to exactly one declared Approval Requirement or child Approval Group, subject to the N_OF_M member restriction in APPROVAL-QUORUM-007.
  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-005 — An Approval Group MUST NOT contain the same member identifier more than once within that group.
  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-006 — An Approval Group MUST NOT create a cycle through child group references.
  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-007 — Nested Approval Group evaluation MUST be bounded to a maximum depth of four groups on every root-to-child path. The standalone root group, or each group directly referenced by a Stage, MUST count as depth one; each child group MUST increase depth by one. Stage and stage-list containers MUST NOT count as group levels.

Evaluation inputs and applicability

  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-008 — Composition evaluation MUST be deterministic from the composition definition, declared member order, current-effective Approval Requirement or Decision observations, and explicit evaluation context.
  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-009 — A declared Requirement member with unresolved applicability MUST fail composition evaluation with FINKORE_APPROVAL_CONDITION_UNRESOLVED; it MUST NOT be treated as approved, rejected, pending, or not applicable.
  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-010 — A required member with missing or malformed current state or effectiveness evidence MUST fail composition evaluation with FINKORE_APPROVAL_INVALID_CHAIN; it MUST NOT be silently inferred. Missing or malformed required evaluation context instead MUST use FINKORE_APPROVAL_INVALID_CONTEXT as defined by Approval Validity. When failures coexist, the returned code MUST follow APPROVAL-ERROR-010.
  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-011 — A member explicitly evaluated as not applicable MUST be omitted from its containing group's outcome evaluation and MUST NOT contribute an approval, rejection, or pending blocker. This includes a child Approval Group with no applicable members after explicit applicability evaluation; the omission MUST propagate through nested groups.
  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-012 — A structurally valid Approval Group with no applicable members after explicit applicability evaluation MUST evaluate as APPROVED, meaning it imposes no current approval obligation. When it is a child group, its containing group MUST treat it as not applicable under APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-011, not as an approving member.

Group outcomes

  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-013 — An ALL_OF group with at least one applicable member MUST evaluate as APPROVED only when every applicable member is approved; it MUST evaluate as REJECTED when any applicable member is rejected; otherwise it MUST evaluate as PENDING.
  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-014 — An ANY_OF group with at least one applicable member MUST evaluate as APPROVED when at least one applicable member is approved; it MUST evaluate as REJECTED only when every applicable member is rejected; otherwise it MUST evaluate as PENDING.
  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-015 — A PENDING member or voter MUST NOT be interpreted as an abstention, rejection, or approval.

Stage ordering and actionability

  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-016 — An ordered Approval Stage list MUST evaluate stages in declared order and MUST NOT make a later stage actionable before every earlier stage is approved.
  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-017 — Groups declared within the same Approval Stage MUST be parallel for composition purposes. Their order MUST determine deterministic observation order only and MUST NOT establish prerequisite ordering.
  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-018 — A staged composition MUST evaluate as APPROVED only when every stage is approved, REJECTED when the first non-approved stage is rejected, and PENDING when the first non-approved stage is pending.
  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-019 — A pending staged composition MUST report all and only the pending, applicable Requirements reachable through exclusively pending groups in its first pending stage. It MUST visit that stage's root groups in declared order and recursively visit each pending group's members in declared order, reporting each Requirement identifier once at its first eligible occurrence. It MUST exclude later stages and approved, rejected, or entirely inapplicable group branches. An approved or rejected composition MUST report no actionable Requirements.

Evidence and complete validation

  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-020 — Composition state observations MUST NOT be treated as proof of which Approval Decision satisfied a Requirement or which subject facts were bound to that Decision.
  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-021 — Composition evaluation MUST reuse Core 2.0 current-effectiveness semantics for withdrawn, expired, superseded, stale-fact, stale-revision, and ineligible Decisions.
  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-022 — A structurally valid Approval Composition with no applicable Approval Requirements after explicit applicability evaluation MUST return APPROVED, meaning no approval is currently required. That outcome MUST NOT create or imply an approving Decision; it MUST remain distinguishable from evidence that a voter approved.
  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-023 — An Approval Stage MUST omit entirely inapplicable groups from its outcome evaluation. With at least one applicable group, the stage MUST evaluate as APPROVED when every applicable group is approved, REJECTED when any applicable group is rejected, and PENDING otherwise. A structurally valid stage with no applicable groups MUST evaluate as APPROVED, meaning it imposes no current approval obligation and does not itself block progression to a later stage.
  • APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-024 — Composition evaluation MUST validate the entire composition definition, applicability of every declared Requirement member, and all required current-state and effectiveness evidence before returning an outcome. This MUST include later stages and all alternative branches, even when their outcome would not change the aggregate result. An otherwise decisive approval, rejection, pending state, or no-obligation result MUST NOT suppress a required validation failure. Validation of a later stage MUST NOT make it actionable.

Quorum rules

  • APPROVAL-QUORUM-001 — An N_OF_M group MUST declare a positive integer threshold N, and N MUST be less than or equal to the number of distinct declared voting members M, counted before applicability evaluation. Evaluation MUST NOT lower or otherwise change N when fewer members apply.
  • APPROVAL-QUORUM-002 — A quorum approval count MUST include only distinct declared voter identities from currently effective approving Decisions that identify the member's referenced Requirement and declared voter Actor; each deciding Actor MUST also be eligible for that Requirement.
  • APPROVAL-QUORUM-003 — A voter identity MUST contribute at most one approval to the same quorum group, even if multiple effective approving Decisions by that voter are present.
  • APPROVAL-QUORUM-004 — Withdrawn, expired, superseded, stale-fact, stale-revision, ineligible, malformed, and rejected Decisions MUST NOT increase a quorum approval count.
  • APPROVAL-QUORUM-005 — An N_OF_M group MUST evaluate as APPROVED when the distinct effective approval count is greater than or equal to N.
  • APPROVAL-QUORUM-006 — An N_OF_M group with at least one explicitly applicable voting member whose threshold is not met MUST evaluate as REJECTED when the number of distinct effective approvals plus remaining pending applicable voting members is less than the declared N; otherwise it MUST evaluate as PENDING.
  • APPROVAL-QUORUM-007 — Each N_OF_M member MUST reference an Approval Requirement and MUST explicitly declare exactly one voter Actor identity; it MUST NOT reference a child Approval Group or leave voter identity to be inferred from subsequent Decisions, a role, or a group.
  • APPROVAL-QUORUM-008 — An N_OF_M group MUST NOT declare the same voter Actor identity in more than one member, even when those members reference different Requirements. This definition constraint applies before applicability evaluation.
  • APPROVAL-QUORUM-009 — For an applicable quorum member, currently effective eligible Decisions by its declared voter for its referenced Requirement and current subject context MUST NOT include both satisfying and rejecting outcomes under that Requirement's outcome mapping. Such opposing evidence MUST fail composition evaluation with FINKORE_APPROVAL_INVALID_CHAIN in the state/effectiveness evidence category of APPROVAL-ERROR-010. Evaluation MUST NOT resolve the conflict by Decision order, timestamp order, or an implicit preference for approval or rejection; only explicit lifecycle or current-effectiveness evidence may remove it. Repeated effective Decisions with the same mapped outcome MUST NOT by themselves constitute conflicting evidence.
  • APPROVAL-QUORUM-010 — Each applicable quorum member's state MUST be determined only from currently effective eligible Decisions matching its declared voter, referenced Requirement, and current subject context, using the Requirement's declared outcome mapping. After required validation, at least one satisfying Decision with no rejecting Decision MUST give that member APPROVED; at least one rejecting Decision with no satisfying Decision MUST give it REJECTED; no effective matching Decision MUST give it PENDING. Quorum capacity and actionable-member selection MUST use this member-specific state; another Actor's Decision or an aggregate Requirement observation MUST NOT replace it.

Quorum Member Evidence

The member state in APPROVAL-QUORUM-010 is an observation for this composition, not a mutation of the referenced Requirement. A Requirement may admit several eligible Actors while a quorum member names only one. An effective rejection by Bob cannot reject Alice's member, just as Bob's approval cannot supply her vote. In that case Alice remains pending if she has no effective matching Decision. If the same Requirement is referenced through another declared voter elsewhere, that occurrence uses its own matching evidence. Actionable Requirement reporting still deduplicates identifiers at their first eligible occurrence under APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-019; it does not assign voters or authorize an action.

Opposing effective Decisions from the same member's voter are invalid evidence, even if other voters already meet N or an alternative group already approves. Complete validation and error priority still apply. A withdrawn, expired, superseded, stale, or otherwise ineffective Decision does not create an effective conflict, but remains in history. Duplicate effective approvals supply one vote; duplicate effective rejections produce one rejected member, not extra votes. No Decision is implicitly withdrawn, superseded, or selected by its timestamp.

This rule governs Core 2.0 quorum evaluation; it does not redefine a standalone Requirement or Approval Chain evaluator.

Threshold Validation and Evaluation

M is the size of the declared electorate, not its currently applicable subset. For example, a two-of-three definition remains structurally valid when only one of its three members applies. Its threshold remains two. With one applicable voter it evaluates as REJECTED, even if that voter approves, because two approvals are unreachable from the current applicable membership.

A REJECTED quorum is an aggregate evaluation outcome; it does not invent a rejected Decision or change any member's evidence. A pending member remains pending even when the overall quorum cannot reach its threshold. Evaluation uses current evidence and does not predict future applicability changes.

When all members are explicitly inapplicable, APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-012 applies: the quorum imposes no current obligation, and its standalone group outcome is APPROVED. If nested, it contributes no member outcome to its parent. The declared threshold remains unchanged; no votes are inferred and N is not reduced to zero.

Entirely Inapplicable Groups

Applicability is separate from approval evidence. A group whose members are all explicitly inapplicable imposes no obligation. Such a child is omitted before its parent combines applicable member outcomes. If this leaves the parent with no applicable members, the same rule applies recursively.

For example, ANY_OF(inapplicable-group, pending-review) remains PENDING, and ANY_OF(inapplicable-group, rejected-review) is REJECTED. The inapplicable branch cannot satisfy either parent. A structurally valid composition in which all Requirements are explicitly inapplicable returns APPROVED, signifying no current approval obligation rather than any approving Decision.

A group with zero declared members is still structurally invalid under APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-004. Explicitly inapplicable members are different from missing applicability facts or missing required state evidence; neither kind of missing evidence establishes an exemption. Existing error rules still apply.

Stage Structure and Depth

A staged composition declares at least one stage, and every stage declares at least one root group. A single Requirement can occupy a stage through a declared ALL_OF group containing that Requirement. A stage with no declared groups is invalid; a stage whose declared groups all become explicitly inapplicable remains valid and follows APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-023.

Count nesting independently from each root group in each stage. Four group levels are permitted; a fifth is rejected. A stage is a sequencing container, not an implicit extra group level, and depth is not accumulated across stages. Requirements are group members, not another group level. The same four-level limit applies to a standalone root. Reference and cycle constraints still apply.

Stage Outcomes

Applicable groups in the same stage combine with ALL_OF semantics, while remaining parallel: their declaration order does not create prerequisites between those groups. Alternatives are expressed inside an explicit ANY_OF group. For example, a stage containing ANY_OF(manager-review, cfo-review) and finance-review requires both the any-of group's approval and finance approval.

One rejected applicable group rejects its stage even if another group is pending. An entirely inapplicable group contributes nothing to the stage. If no groups apply, the valid stage imposes no current obligation and does not block progress; it does not imply that any voter approved. Earlier non-approved stages still block later-stage action under APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-016.

APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-018 continues to determine the overall staged outcome from the first non-approved stage. A pending earlier stage and a rejected later stage therefore give a PENDING staged outcome when the input observations are valid. All required later-stage evidence is validated under APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-024. Selection of a portable error when multiple validation failures coexist follows APPROVAL-ERROR-010 in Approval Errors.

Actionable Requirements

For a pending staged composition, select its first pending stage and descend only through groups whose current outcome is PENDING. Report each pending, applicable Requirement once, at its first eligible occurrence in recursive declared order. An earlier occurrence inside an approved or rejected branch is not eligible and does not suppress a later eligible occurrence. This is a reporting order, not a prerequisite ordering between parallel groups.

For a stage containing ANY_OF(A, B) and a group containing C, if A is approved and B and C are pending, only C is actionable. If A and B are both pending and the any-of group is pending, both are available alternatives. A pending quorum can likewise expose more candidates than the number of additional votes needed; the list does not mean every candidate must approve. Group outcome rules still determine satisfaction.

A rejected group can contain pending leaves, but that branch contributes no current actionable Requirements. Approved, rejected, and entirely inapplicable compositions report none. Actionability is an observation of current approval obligations, not authorization, assignment, or permission to bypass eligibility. Complete validation still applies before this report is returned.

Complete Validation

"Entire composition definition" in APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-024 includes groups disconnected from the standalone root or every stage root. Every declared member reference resolves under APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-004, and every declared component is cycle-free under APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-006. A disconnected self-cycle, multi-group cycle, or missing child is invalid structure in category 1 of APPROVAL-ERROR-010. A valid unused group remains permitted. Validation does not give that group an outcome contribution or actionable Requirements.

The depth-four bound in APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-007 measures paths from declared standalone/stage roots, including each path to a shared child. Checking cycles throughout the declaration does not make each unused group an evaluation root or impose a depth bound on unreachable paths. Applicability and required evidence for every declared Requirement member remain subject to complete validation, including members in disconnected groups.

For an applicable quorum member, eligibility and both outcome mappings are required evidence under APPROVAL-QUORUM-002/010 and APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-010. A voter declaration supplies an identity, not evidence of eligibility. Missing, null, or malformed required eligibility/mapping evidence uses FINKORE_APPROVAL_INVALID_CHAIN in category 4 of APPROVAL-ERROR-010, after structure, applicability, and required context. These checks apply even with no votes or a decisive result elsewhere. Explicit inapplicability requires no vote or quorum eligibility/mapping evidence; supplied malformed evidence is not repaired. The bounded fixture is specified in conformance conventions. No concrete subject schema is added to lightweight composition observations.

Required evaluation instants use SPEC-TIMESTAMP-001 through SPEC-TIMESTAMP-006; mere member presence or a nonempty string is not timestamp validation. In the bounded fixture, an applicable observation declaring requiresEvaluationContext: true requires a valid context.evaluatedAt. Absent, null, malformed, calendar-invalid, or excessive-precision values use FINKORE_APPROVAL_INVALID_CONTEXT in category 3 of APPROVAL-ERROR-010. Valid timestamps retain their original spelling and exact instant semantics. This does not require time context on observations that do not require it.

Before any composition outcome is returned, validate all declared structure and required observations, including later stages and alternative branches that would otherwise be unnecessary to the result. An approved ANY_OF branch cannot hide unresolved applicability or missing required state in another branch. Likewise, a pending or rejected early stage cannot hide a malformed later-stage group.

Complete validation is an observable guarantee, not a required implementation architecture or an obligation to collect all errors. An evaluator may stop and return a validation error; it cannot stop checking required inputs and return an outcome merely because that outcome seems determined. The error returned must respect the category priority in APPROVAL-ERROR-010 even when validation can stop before collecting every defect.

An explicit valid PENDING observation is different from missing required state. An applicable Requirement with no effective Decision legitimately remains PENDING; validation must not fabricate a Decision merely to supply evidence. Explicit inapplicability removes the approval obligation, not structural validity or the need to establish applicability. It does not require an approving Decision.

Likewise, an explicitly ineffective Decision differs from a supplied Decision whose required effectiveness evidence is absent or malformed. Under APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-010 and APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-024, the latter is invalid evidence, not an effective vote or an instruction to silently discard the Decision. It uses FINKORE_APPROVAL_INVALID_CHAIN in category 4 of APPROVAL-ERROR-010, even if another branch already supplies enough votes. An empty, valid set of effective Decisions can still leave a member pending. The conformance fixture represents each supplied Decision's effectiveness with an explicit Boolean; this encoding is not a new production serialization requirement.

Validation observes current input; it does not activate future stages, request votes, mutate history, or resolve missing facts through ambient lookup. The current stage's actionability is determined separately by the stage rules.

Invariants

Approval Composition is an observation over Approval Requirements and current effective Approval Decision evidence. It does not create Approval Decisions, authorize Actors, resolve dynamic approvers, or mutate Approval history.

Composition must not count ineffective evidence. A historical Approval Decision can remain committed while contributing nothing to a current group, quorum, or stage because its facts changed, its subject revision changed, it expired, it was withdrawn, it was superseded, or its Requirement was superseded.

Examples

ALL_OF(manager-review, finance-review)
ANY_OF(finance-manager-review, cfo-review)
N_OF_M(2, board-member-a, board-member-b, board-member-c)
DECLARED STAGE GROUPS:
  manager-group = ALL_OF(manager-review)
  finance-options = ANY_OF(controller-review, finance-review)
  cfo-group = ALL_OF(cfo-review)
STAGES:
  1. manager-group
  2. finance-options
  3. cfo-group

For the quorum example, board-member-a, board-member-b, and board-member-c reference Requirements and declare distinct voters Alice, Bob, and Carol, respectively. Effective eligible approvals from Alice and Bob supply two votes. Repeated approving Decisions from Alice supply at most one vote. A Decision by another Actor cannot contribute to Alice's member even if that Actor is eligible for the referenced Requirement.

ALL_OF(finance-review, board-quorum) can combine a finance Requirement with that quorum. N_OF_M(2, finance-group, board-group) is invalid because child Group outcomes are not voting members.

The examples are illustrative. They do not define a production serialization.

Invalid Examples

  • Counting one Actor twice toward the same quorum.
  • Accepting opposing effective votes from one declared voter by taking the latest timestamp, the first encountered Decision, approval, or rejection.
  • Treating another eligible Actor's rejection as the named voter's rejection.
  • Hiding conflicting effective votes because another branch already approves.
  • Declaring Alice as the voter for two members of one quorum, even if one member later evaluates as not applicable.
  • Declaring a quorum member as “anyone from Finance” without one explicit voter.
  • Counting a child group as a quorum vote.
  • Lowering a two-of-three threshold to one because only one member applies.
  • Rejecting a valid declared quorum definition as malformed solely because fewer members currently apply than its threshold.
  • Treating a withdrawn or expired Decision as a current approval.
  • Making the CFO stage actionable before the manager stage is approved.
  • Accepting a nested group cycle.
  • Treating a missing member state as PENDING or NOT_APPLICABLE.
  • Using an entirely inapplicable child as the approving branch of ANY_OF.
  • Approving a stage because one parallel group approved while another applicable group remains pending or rejected.
  • Requiring an approving Decision for an entirely inapplicable stage.
  • Recording an approving Decision because a composition has no applicable requirements.
  • Treating an empty declaration as a valid all-inapplicable group.
  • Declaring an empty stage list or a stage without declared root groups.
  • Returning APPROVED from ANY_OF before checking another branch's required state or applicability.
  • Returning PENDING because an early stage is pending while a later stage has a validation failure.
  • Making a later stage actionable solely because its evidence was validated.
  • Reporting a pending leaf inside an already approved or rejected group as actionable through that branch.
  • Reporting the same actionable Requirement twice or sorting identifiers instead of preserving recursive declared order.
  • Treating all reported ANY_OF alternatives as mandatory approvals.
  • Accepting five nested groups beneath a stage because only child levels were counted, or rejecting four because the stage container was counted as a group.

Errors

Invalid group shape, an empty stage list or stage without declared groups, invalid threshold shape, missing or conflicting required member evidence, duplicate members or quorum voter identities, quorum members without exactly one explicit voter or referencing child groups, unresolved references, cycles, and excessive nesting use FINKORE_APPROVAL_INVALID_CHAIN.

A structurally valid quorum with at least one applicable member whose threshold is unreachable evaluates as REJECTED; reduced applicability alone is not an invalid-threshold error. A non-positive or non-integer N, or N greater than the declared M, is an invalid definition using FINKORE_APPROVAL_INVALID_CHAIN.

Unresolved applicability uses FINKORE_APPROVAL_CONDITION_UNRESOLVED. Missing or malformed required current-effectiveness context uses FINKORE_APPROVAL_INVALID_CONTEXT, including a missing evaluation instant for an expiring Decision. Coexisting failures follow APPROVAL-ERROR-010: structure, applicability, required context, then required state/effectiveness evidence.

A domain action blocked by a pending or rejected required composition uses FINKORE_APPROVAL_REQUIRED unless a composing domain defines a more specific already-specified failure.

Non-Goals

This document does not define delegation, escalation, IAM/RBAC, authorization, actor-directory lookup, dynamic approver resolution, notification or inbox behavior, persistence, workflow migration, arbitrary graph traversal, executable callbacks, or a portable condition expression language.
